answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 7 times its size, so a group of 7 keys loses far more than 7 single identities would. The beacon graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the juniper audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the anchor checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
